title: The manhole cover that left Earth
caption:
America may have launched a manhole cover faster than any rocket ever built. By accident. With a nuke. 🚀
An underground blast turned a 150 m shaft into a gun barrel: hot gas punched the 900 kg steel lid out at an estimated 66 km/s.
Did it reach space, or burn up in seconds? Pick a side.
first_comment: The first object humans sent past escape velocity was a manhole cover. Change my mind 🛸
sources: Operation Plumbbob, shot Pascal-B, Nevada Test Site, 27 August 1957: a low-yield device at the bottom of a ~150 m (500 ft) shaft capped with a ~900 kg (2,000 lb) steel/iron lid (US DOE Nevada nuclear test history; Wikipedia 'Operation Plumbbob')

Robert Brownlee (Los Alamos), 'Learning to Contain Underground Nuclear Explosions' (2002): the lid appeared in only one high-speed camera frame; his estimate of about 66 km/s, roughly six times Earth's escape velocity; the lid was never found and probably burned up or broke up in the atmosphere
